chapters.title: Chapter 2: How Each Component Is Taxed

lessons.title: Allowances and Reimbursements: LTA, Meals, Phone, Fuel and Books

children.text: Kiran, a product lead at a Bengaluru fintech, opens her company's "flexi benefits" portal in April. It offers meal vouchers, phone and internet reimbursement, fuel reimbursement, LTA, books and periodicals, and gift cards. Her colleague says it is all a waste in the new regime. Another says it saves him ₹60,000 a year.

They are both partly right. After the Income-tax Rules, 2026, some of these items are tax-free in both regimes, some only in the old regime, and some only if you keep the right bills. This lesson sorts them out, one by one.

body.text: An allowance is taxed by what it is. A reimbursement is taxed by what you can prove.

children.text: Allowance, reimbursement or perquisite?
Allowance
: a fixed sum paid every month, whether or not you spend it. Taxable unless a specific exemption applies.

markDefs.definition: A fixed amount paid with salary for a stated purpose, whether or not you spend it. It is taxable unless a specific exemption applies.

children.text: Reimbursement
: repayment of an actual expense against bills. If the expense is genuinely for work, it is not your income at all.

markDefs.definition: Repayment by the employer of an expense you actually incurred for work, against bills. Genuine official expense reimbursements are not treated as your income.

children.text: Perquisite
: a benefit in kind such as meal vouchers, gift cards or the use of a car, taxed at a value set by the Income-tax Rules, 2026 under Section 17 of the Income-tax Act, 2025.

body.title: Label beats intention
body.question: Rakesh gets a "Telephone Allowance" of ₹2,000 a month, paid with salary. He never submits bills. How is it taxed in the new regime?
options: Fully exempt, phone costs are work-related
Exempt only if he uses the phone for work
body.explanation: A fixed allowance paid without bills is simply salary with a label. Phone and internet costs are tax-free only when your employer reimburses actual bills for a connection used for work. The same ₹2,000, paid as a bill-based reimbursement, would not be taxed.

children.text: Leave Travel Allowance (old regime only)

LTA exempts the cost of travel within India for you and your family while on leave, under Section 11 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 10(5) of the 1961 Act). It is one of the most generous old-regime exemptions, and one of the most restricted.

cells: 2 journeys in a block of 4 calendar years. Current block: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2029
Within India only. International trips do not qualify, even for the domestic leg
Travel fare only. Hotels, food, sightseeing and local taxis are not covered
Up to the economy fare of the national carrier by the shortest route
Up to the AC First Class fare by the shortest route
You, your spouse, your children, and parents and siblings wholly or mainly dependent on you
Maximum 2 children born after 1 October 1998, except for multiple births after the first child
Lower of the LTA component you receive and the eligible fare actually spent

body.title: LTA blocks and the carry-forward window

events.title: New block begins
events.description: Two fresh journeys available until 31 December 2029.

events.title: Carry-forward deadline
events.description: If you used fewer than two journeys in 2022 to 2025, one unused journey can be claimed in 2026 only, in addition to the two in the new block.

events.title: Block ends
events.description: Unused journeys lapse, except one that can be carried into calendar year 2030.

children.text: Meera, in the old regime, has LTA of ₹60,000 in her CTC. In December 2026 she flies from Chennai to Jaipur with her husband and two children. Economy return fares for four cost ₹48,000 and the hotel costs ₹20,000. Her exemption is ₹48,000, the fare. The remaining ₹12,000 of LTA is taxable, and the hotel does not count at all.

body.title: Harish's Kerala trip
body.prompt: Harish, in the old regime, receives LTA of ₹50,000. He takes his wife and dependent mother from Delhi to Kochi. Economy air fares come to ₹36,000, airport taxis ₹4,000 and the houseboat ₹15,000. How much of his LTA is exempt?
body.explanation: Only the fare counts: ₹36,000. Taxis and the houseboat are not travel fare. Exempt LTA = lower of ₹50,000 received and ₹36,000 eligible fare = ₹36,000. The remaining ₹14,000 is taxable.

children.text: Meal vouchers: now worth up to ₹1,05,600 a year, in both regimes

The Income-tax Rules, 2026 raised the tax-free value of employer-provided meals, including meal vouchers and cards, from ₹50 to ₹200 per meal. Unlike most items in this lesson, this works in the new regime too.

body.label: Maximum tax-free meal vouchers a year
body.context: ₹200 × 2 meals a day × 22 working days × 12 months. At the 30% slab plus cess, that saves ₹32,947 of tax in either regime.

children.text: Meals must be for working days and during working hours
Vouchers must be non-transferable and usable only for food and non-alcoholic drinks
Any value above ₹200 per meal is taxable
Vouchers you do not use are still valued at their face value, so choose a realistic amount
Gifts and vouchers: ₹15,000 a year
Non-cash gifts, gift cards and vouchers from your employer are tax-free up to a total of ₹15,000 in the tax year, up from ₹5,000. Cash gifts and anything convertible to cash are fully taxable.

body.title: Diwali and year-end gifts
body.textWithBlank: Pooja gets an ₹8,000 Diwali gift card and a ₹10,000 year-end voucher from her employer. The taxable part is ₹___.
body.explanation: Total non-cash gifts = ₹18,000. The first ₹15,000 is tax-free, so ₹3,000 is added to her taxable salary. This works the same in both regimes.

children.text: Phone and internet: bills, not allowances

Reimbursement of your mobile and broadband bills is not treated as a taxable perquisite, and this continues in the new regime because it is not an exemption being claimed, it is simply not income. The catch is paperwork: the reimbursement must be against actual bills, generally for a connection used for work. If your employer reimburses ₹1,500 of bills a month, that is ₹18,000 a year out of your taxable salary.
Fuel and car running costs
Many flexi plans let you claim fuel, maintenance and driver costs for your own car. The Income-tax Rules, 2026 sharply raised the amounts used to value this.

body.caption: Your own car, employer reimburses running costs, tax year 2026-27

cells: Only for official work, with a log book and employer certificate
Official and personal use, engine up to 1.6 litres or electric
₹5,000 a month treated as official use. Reimbursement above that is taxable
Official and personal use, engine above 1.6 litres
₹7,000 a month treated as official use. Reimbursement above that is taxable
Driver provided or reimbursed, mixed use
A further ₹3,000 a month treated as official use
Only personal use, including only home to office

children.text: Example: Kiran drives a 1.2 litre hatchback for client visits and personal use. Her employer reimburses ₹12,000 of fuel and maintenance bills a month. ₹5,000 a month (₹60,000 a year) is treated as official use, and ₹7,000 a month (₹84,000 a year) is added to her taxable salary. Earlier rules used ₹1,800 a month for the same car.

body.text: Payroll teams do not all apply these car valuation rules the same way, and the 2026 figures are new. Before building a large fuel reimbursement into your flexi plan, ask payroll exactly how much of it they will treat as taxable, and keep fuel bills and a travel log.

children.text: Books, uniforms and other old-regime allowances

cells: Books and periodicals (against bills, for work)
Exempt to the extent spent on uniforms for work
Up to ₹3,000 a month per child, max 2
Up to ₹9,000 a month per child, max 2
Conveyance for official duties, tour and transfer travel, daily allowance on tour
Transport allowance for specified disabled employees
Up to ₹15,000 plus DA a month in the 8 listed cities, ₹8,000 plus DA elsewhere
Phone and internet reimbursement against bills

children.text: Kiran builds her flexi basket

Kiran is in the new regime, and her taxable income stays above ₹24,00,000 even after these choices, so every rupee moved out of taxable salary saves 31.2% (30% plus 4% cess). She moves part of her special allowance into the items that still work in the new regime.

body.title: Kiran's tax-free flexi basket: ₹1,98,600 a year

data.label: Car running costs treated as official

stats.label: Tax-free basket
stats.context: Per year, in the new regime

stats.label: Skipped
stats.context: Taxable in the new regime, so no benefit

body.title: Build a basket for Arjun
body.scenario: Arjun, 32, is a sales manager in Pune on the new regime, with taxable income around ₹18,00,000. His flexi plan lets him allocate up to ₹2,40,000 a year across: meal vouchers, LTA, books and periodicals, phone and internet reimbursement, fuel for his own 1.5 litre car, and gift vouchers. He uses his car heavily for client visits and personally on weekends, spends about ₹1,200 a month on his phone, and eats lunch at office on working days. Anything he does not allocate stays as taxable special allowance.
body.prompt: How should Arjun allocate his ₹2,40,000, and what must he do to keep it tax-free?
body.modelAnswer: Skip LTA and books: both are taxable in the new regime, so they add paperwork for no saving. Meal vouchers: he eats one meal a day at work, so ₹200 × 22 × 12 = ₹52,800 is realistic. Allocating more than he uses wastes nothing tax-wise only if the vouchers are genuinely consumed, so keep it honest. Phone: ₹1,200 × 12 = ₹14,400 against bills. Gift vouchers: ₹15,000. Fuel: with a 1.5 litre car used for both work and personal trips, ₹5,000 a month (₹60,000 a year) can be treated as official use, so allocate about that much, backed by fuel bills. Total tax-free: ₹52,800 + ₹14,400 + ₹15,000 + ₹60,000 = ₹1,42,200. The remaining ₹97,800 stays taxable. With taxable income around ₹18 lakh, he is in the 20% slab, so the saving is about ₹1,42,200 × 20.8% = ₹29,578. He must submit bills on time, keep a basic travel log for the car, and confirm with payroll how they value the car reimbursement.

body.title: Keep your reimbursements tax-free
steps: Submit phone and internet bills in your own name for every month claimed
Keep fuel and maintenance bills and a simple log of official trips
Choose meal voucher amounts you will genuinely use on working days
Keep gift vouchers from your employer within ₹15,000 for the year
For LTA in the old regime, keep tickets and boarding passes, and note which block journey you are using
Check your Form 16 to see which reimbursements payroll treated as taxable

body.text: Limits reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026 for tax year 2026-27. Employer flexi plans, documentation standards and payroll interpretations vary. This lesson is for education and is not personalised tax advice.

points: Fixed allowances are taxable unless a specific exemption applies. Reimbursements of genuine work expenses against bills are not income.
LTA covers only domestic travel fare, 2 journeys in the 2026 to 2029 block, and only in the old regime.
Meal vouchers are tax-free up to ₹200 per meal and gifts up to ₹15,000 a year, in both regimes.
Phone and internet reimbursement against bills stays tax-free in the new regime.
For your own car used for work and personal trips, ₹5,000 a month (₹7,000 above 1.6 litres, plus ₹3,000 for a driver) is treated as official use.
In the new regime, skip LTA, books and education allowances in your flexi plan. They save nothing.
